title: Catalyst MedTech — field deployment digest
content:
Quick context: Catalyst MedTech (CM) builds a clinic-side triage assistant used by nurses to capture patient symptoms and surface likely next-steps. They have strict PHI rules and want a private deployment in their Azure VNet with optional air-gapped mode for certain facilities. Met with CM engineering + security on 2025-02-14. Notes below are my working capture — raw, action-oriented.

Meeting snapshot (attendees):
- CM: Dr. Elena Soto (CTO), Amir Basri (infra lead), Layla Ortiz (compliance)
- Redwood: Jordan Rivera (solutions), Priya Nair (private deployments), Marcus Li (SRE)

What they said they need (high level):
- Private VPC deployment with zero PHI leaving customer network (BAA required).
- KMS/HSM integration for keys; some facilities will require on-prem HSM.
- Model pinning & deterministic rollouts (no surprise model swaps).
- Latency SLO: 95th < 250ms for short prompts (triage forms ~50–150 tokens).
- Throughput: expected 20 concurrent nurses per clinic during peak; plan for 8 clinics in region 1 (burst to 200 across clusters).
- Fallback behavior: degrade to smaller model locally if primary is unavailable; full-feature call to hosted not allowed for PHI.
- Local logging/audit trail with tamper-evident retention for 7 years (compliance asks).

Environment constraints / gotchas they mentioned / we flagged: 
- On-prem GPU fleet is mixed: some nodes are A10s, a handful of older V100s. Quantization & kernel selection will be critical to hit latency SLOs on A10. V100s likely need smaller model variant or lower-throughput routing.
- Intermittent network to regional SAN: cannot rely on remote model cache warmups that require cloud access. Need robust cold-start behavior and persistent KV cache persisted locally.
- Strict egress rules: CM will block outbound to non-approved endpoints. We'll need IP allowlist + offline installers for agents.
- HSM variety: some sites use Azure Key Vault HSM; others have Thales on-prem HSM behind a jump box. Integration testing will be slow; plan for a hardware test matrix.
- PHI scrub rules: they want explicit deterministic redaction option before any tokenization storage. This complicates evals/quality monitoring (we cannot keep raw prompts in observability pipeline without their approval).
- Monitoring retention: security wants raw traces only kept behind their sysadmin, but Redwood console will need to ingest aggregated metrics. Need a contract clause about sampled telemetry only.

Technical considerations / proposed config:
- Deploy Redwood Private VPC appliance per region; each appliance pinned to a model bundle (customer-owned model versions + Redwood-open model variants).
- Default runtime config: 8xA10-equivalent serving threads per node, dynamic batching disabled for low-latency endpoints (use continuous batching with max latency 30ms to avoid tail). Evaluate enabling tiny-batch mode for throughput windows.
- KV cache persisted to local NVMe and snapshot export to on-prem object store nightly. This mitigates cold-start risk when restarting pods.
- Model quantization: recommend 4-bit quantization for primary model variant (run bench on A10, if V100s fail SLO, route those nodes to int8 distillation variant).
- Rollout policy: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% within cluster; default fallback to smaller local model if primary fails health checks for >30s. No external-hosted fallback allowed for PHI.
- Auth: mutual TLS between agent and control plane; initial bootstrap via offline token signed by CM PKI.

Open questions we must answer for CM security team:
1) Can Redwood support fully offline HSM attestation flow (no outbound)? If not, which parts require outbound connectivity?
2) Exact audit log format and proof-of-integrity mechanism — CM wants tamper-evident logs and verifiable hashes; will Redwood provide signed digests on a schedule?
3) Data residency: can observability export strip prompt text at source and only send token counts + timing + error codes? Need a sample pipeline description.
4) Failure modes: if NVMe snapshot is corrupt after power event, what are restoration guarantees and RPO/RTO?

Action items / owners / rough timeline (working):
- Action: Draft security checklist + BAA addendum for CM. Owner: Priya. Due: 2025-02-21. (PRIYA: include clause on sampled telemetry and offline installer checklist).
- Action: Run perf matrix on A10 vs V100 with candidate model (triage model v1.0). Owner: Marcus. Due: 2025-02-20. Deliverable: single-sheet latency/throughput table and recommended quantization config.
- Action: Proof-of-concept installer (air-gapped) + bootstrap flow doc. Owner: Jordan. Due: 2025-02-28. Include MD5/sha256 signing steps and manual key injection steps.
- Action: Compliance sign-off checklist (Layla + Redwood security). Owner: Layla (CM) + Redwood security (TBD). Target: 2025-03-10.
- Action: Create sample redaction pipeline for triage forms (pre-tokenization redaction heuristics + allowlist for structured fields). Owner: Jordan + eng-applied-ml. Due: 2025-03-04.

Risks / contingency notes:
- If V100 nodes dominate certain clinics, they may not meet 250ms 95th* without reducing model size or increasing node count. Need to surface cost tradeoff early.
- HSM integration delays could block test deployments for 2–6 weeks depending on vendor cooperation. Plan to run cryptographic mocking mode for early functional tests (explicitly documented).
- Telemetry constraints could reduce our ability to detect subtle regressions; propose a telemetry beta where CM allows limited redacted fields for first 8 weeks.

Notes-to-self (raw):
- Prepare sample workload: 60k prompts/day per clinic assumption -> multiply for 8 clinics -> 480k/day -> useful for cost estimates.
- Create small eval set derived from their sample triage forms (anonymize and get Layla sign-off).
- Check if Legal needs a DMZ clause for the offline installer thumbdrive transfer.
- Ask infra: do we have signed offline installers in current repo? If not, schedule build step.

Meeting follow-up prep (what to send CM within 24–48h):
1) Short one-pager: deployment options + quick cost/lifecycle summary.
2) Perf summary table (Marcus will supply) + recommended model variant mapping to GPU type.
3) Security checklist / BAA draft (Priya).
4) PoC installer walkthrough doc + expected test plan (Jordan).

Slack next steps: post perf question in #infra-tools to get David H on kernel tuning. Ping legal for BAA template.

Immediate TODO (today):
- Draft one-pager skeleton (Jordan) and attach perf matrix placeholder.
- Confirm Marcus bench start time and request test model artifact location.

-- end working capture --

Random thoughts / future ideas:
- Consider an on-device lighter assistant that runs in a mobile app for field triage when network is down (no PHI egress). Could be a local distilled policy model that syncs anonymized stats overnight. Worth flagging to product.
- Policy: add explicit contract option for sampled telemetry + opt-in extended observability for first 60 days to help guardrail regressions.
